newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street pushes still higher at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street pushes still higher at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks blasted past the 7500 level at midday Tuesday in its third straight session of record-setting highs.
Analysts said there are no major barriers to hold the market back from a prolonged rally. Although some predicted consolidation this afternoon, they also said the climb should continue.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up about 67 points, or 0.89 percent, to 7545.
Earlier in the morning the Dow climbed to a high of 7572.20 before scaling back.
The Nasdaq composite fell back from its earlier rebound and was off 1.68 points to 1410.

Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd, pointed to two major factors contributing to the gains: "The major Dow and S&P averages are on a major technical breakout to new all-time highs; also, money continues to be shoehorned in by foreigners, primarily Europeans, into first-tier stocks."
Beyond this, he said, "people are definitely scratching their heads today."
"The market is just adding to its gains and that will continue as long as there is favorable rotation" among stocks, said Jonathan Dodd, a Dean Witter technical analyst.
Analysts said U.S. investors are starting to rotate their money into second-tier stocks as the first tier nears over-valuation.
"There is no indication that buyers have had their fill," said Alan Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
Analysts said the rally would cool eventually, at least for a pause in the uptrend that started with a 130-point gain on Friday.
Also, the market will soon start focusing on the possibility of an interest rate rise as the July meeting of Federal Reserve grows nearer, they said.
"My suspicion is that the Dow is going to exhaust itself," said Joseph Battipaglia, chief investment officer at Gruntal.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was up 2/32 at a 6.82 percent yield. The Standard & Poor's futures index was up 2.25 at 868.10.
On the New York Stock Exchange, Santa Fe International Corp topped the most active list in its market debut with a gain of 3-7/8 to 32-3/8.
Cypress Semiconductor Corp climbed 1-5/8 to 15-1/8 after being raised by Morgan Stanley to outperform from neutral.
Boeing Co rose 1-3/8 to 57 after announcing a pact to sell 35 aircraft to Continental Airlines.
Ascend Communications Inc shares were battered after the company was downgraded by both UBS Securities and Soundview. The stock fell 5-5/8 to 42.
Cascade Communications Corp, which said it had regulatory approval to merge with Ascend, fell 3-7/8 to 29.
Xylan Corp also stumbled, shedding 2-3/4 to 14-1/2, after warning that its second-quarter results would be lower than those of the first quarter.
((--Wall Street Desk 212-859-1730))
